lead.hed: U.S. and Indian armies closed three weeks of training in India
lead.insight: DVIDS, posted Sunday morning from Auli: U.S. and Indian Army forces closed Exercise Yudh Abhyas 2026 in a ceremony Sept. 27, ending three weeks of bilateral training at Auli and Mahajan Field Firing Range. The 22nd iteration paired the 11th Airborne Division's 1st Mobile Brigade Combat Team with the Indian Army for jungle training, combined air assault, and live fire that included HIMARS. Col. Ben Jackman said the point was soldiers who know each other's equipment if they are ever called to fight together. Official still from the closing formation.
lead.image_credit: 2nd Lt. Hannah Allebaugh · DVIDS 9969156 · Public domain · U.S. and Indian Army soldiers in formation at the Yudh Abhyas 2026 closing ceremony, Auli, India, Sept. 26, 2026.

political.hed: The Air Force says the Grey Wolf helicopter is ready for nuclear-security duty
political.insight: DVIDS, from Air Force Global Strike Command: the MH-139 Grey Wolf reached initial operational capability on Aug. 10, replacing the Vietnam-era UH-1N Huey on missile-field security. The command says the new helicopter is nearly 50 percent faster and can carry twice as many troops. Gen. S.L. Davis called it a significant improvement for securing the land leg of the nuclear triad. Announcement of a readiness milestone, not a new deployment order.

political.hed: A new indictment names Mexican state officials in a cartel case
political.insight: Heritage, Friday: the commentary says the administration shifted from targeting cartel workers to a Justice Department indictment that names ten past and present officials of Mexico's ruling party in Sinaloa, including Governor Rubén Rocha Moya. All ten have denied wrongdoing. Commentary on an indictment, not a new statute. Not a ship story.

political.hed: Treating a child as the opposite sex is not the legal definition of abuse, a report argues
political.insight: Heritage, Friday: institutions built to protect children are under scrutiny after parents lost custody for refusing to treat a gender-confused child as the opposite sex. The report says those cases rest on an ideological premise, not the legal definition of abuse. Report, not a new statute. Not a ship story.

tech.hed: The administration has obligated $307 million of last year's Ukraine military aid
tech.insight: Defense News, Friday, citing Reuters: the administration has made legally binding commitments to spend almost all of the $400 million Congress approved for military aid to Ukraine late last year, so the money will not expire Sept. 30. As of early last week, $307 million of that $400 million was obligated, according to three sources familiar with the plan. Obligation report, not a new appropriation.

tech.hed: An essay says progressive stories took public blows at the end of summer
tech.insight: Law & Liberty, Friday: the essay says it was a rough end of summer for mainstream progressive narratives, and points to congressional hearings on Anthony Fauci's coronavirus statements and to former NBA players challenging the gender-identity claim. Essay, not a statute.

culture.hed: An essay says Xi's pressure on the Chinese church calls for a harder U.S. line
culture.insight: Providence, Thursday: the essay opens on President Trump's June remark at the Faith and Freedom Coalition that he is saving Christians throughout the world, and argues Christians should take that claim seriously when measuring policy toward China. Argument about persecution and U.S. policy, not a new statute.

culture.hed: A third essay takes up the Christian Sabbath
culture.insight: TruthScript, Wednesday, reprinting a Presbyterian Polity piece with the author's permission: the third installment continues a biblical and theological case for the Christian Sabbath begun in the first two articles. Theology essay, not a news event. Not Friday's data-center essay.
